objective: Measure the effect of missing feature values on the frozen v0.2 OOD score, derive feature-family missingness from canonical extraction functions, and preserve the result as a diagnostic without changing production eligibility or model behavior.
previous_knowledge_consumed: The v0.2.0 baseline must preserve the 42-feature schema, feature order, model configuration, class order, and historical cutoff.
PR #279 exposes per-row feature coverage and OOD evaluation basis. It deliberately does not gate partial rows.
The frozen reference matrix has 150 objects, 15 ALeRCE reference classes, and 10 objects per class; 59 rows are complete and 91 are partial.
The feature pipeline uses 10 valid observations for basic per-band features and 30 for Lomb–Scargle features.

Cross-band colors require at least one valid observation in both bands. Sample-standard-deviation variability ratios require at least two observations in the relevant band and both bands must be present.
OOD reference scores are in-sample and reference-relative. They are not calibrated probabilities.
Issue #170 remains unresolved. The CPVS published-membership discrepancy is independent of this OOD work.

baseline.scope: Diagnostic-only experiment. No production model, feature values, feature order, class order, cutoff, scientific gate, or CPVS selection criteria changed.

change.rationale: Quantify OOD score sensitivity to random and extraction-aligned missingness. Verify whether natural missing-feature patterns match the canonical v0.2 extraction eligibility rules. Preserve all results without introducing an arbitrary coverage threshold.

reproducibility.before: No pinned, hash-verified OOD missingness sensitivity experiment or machine-readable feature-family map.
reproducibility.after: MCAR and extraction-aligned masking experiments record input hashes, runtime versions, model configuration, output hashes, and an artifact reference.

coverage.before: Natural missing-feature patterns had not been matched against all canonical v0.2 extraction eligibility rules.
coverage.after: 150/150 rows match an exact extraction-aligned pattern; 91 partial rows have zero unmatched and zero ambiguous patterns.

robustness.before: The effect of missing features on OOD anomaly flags was not measured under MCAR or correlated extraction patterns.
robustness.after: Eight MCAR levels and 17 extraction-aligned scenarios were measured on 59 complete rows. Missingness suppresses existing flags; no new flags were created in the 17 correlated scenarios.

reliability.before: A partial-row OOD score could be emitted without a quantitative description of its missing-feature sensitivity.
reliability.after: The paired experiment shows downward percentile shifts and suppression of baseline anomaly flags, including complete suppression of all baseline 90th/95th/99th flags when both bands have 2–9 observations.

regression_protection_count.evidence: Dedicated experiment workflow run 42698425064; 6 tests passed.

scientific_validity.evidence: No independent astrophysical ID/OOD labels or production-artifact byte comparison are available.

measurement.trade_off: The experiment demonstrates sensitivity and natural missingness provenance. It does not establish a production OOD eligibility threshold, calibrated probability, precision, recall, or population-level validity.

The experiment reconstructs OODProductionModel from the frozen matrix and configuration. It does not load or byte-compare a persisted production artifact.
The experiment reference scores are in-sample. No independent astrophysical OOD labels were used.

root_causes: The 150-object frozen dataset's missing-feature patterns are fully explained by the canonical 10/30 observation thresholds and the 1/2 observation cross-band rules.
Median imputation followed by IsolationForest scoring can lower anomaly scores when feature groups are missing. The paired masking experiment shows that this can suppress baseline anomaly flags.
The current reference set is too small and lacks independent ID/OOD labels to define a general production eligibility policy.
The persisted production OOD artifact is not available in the repository. The reconstructed model cannot establish byte-for-byte artifact parity.
unresolved: Production OOD artifact parity remains unverified.
Independent astrophysical ID/OOD evaluation data are not available.
A versioned, evidence-based OOD eligibility policy is not established.

findings: All 150 natural missing-feature patterns match the v0.2 extraction eligibility rules; no unmatched or ambiguous patterns remain.
The eight objects with 38 missing features have 2–9 valid observations in both bands and retain only four cross-band features.
MCAR and extraction-aligned masking can lower reference-relative OOD percentiles and suppress baseline anomaly flags.
Rank correlation can remain moderate while absolute OOD percentiles move downward. Rank stability alone is not enough to trust a threshold decision.
The 90th, 95th, and 99th percentile thresholds are reference-relative thresholds, not calibrated probabilities.
A partial-feature OOD score must remain explicitly labelled. It must not be presented as equivalent to a complete-feature evaluation.
No fixed coverage threshold is justified by this 150-object reference experiment.
ALeRCE labels are reference labels, not independent astrophysical ground truth.

open_blockers: Independent astrophysical ID/OOD labels are not available.
Production OOD eligibility criteria remain unvalidated.

knowledge_carried_forward: Keep PR #280 diagnostic-only. Do not change the production OOD model, imputer, scaler, classifier, feature schema, class order, or v0.2.0 baseline.
Keep per-row coverage and OOD evaluation-state reporting from PR #279.
Do not suppress partial-row scores or set a fixed coverage threshold without independent validation.
Do not treat OOD percentiles as calibrated probabilities.
Do not use ALeRCE labels as independent astrophysical ground truth.
Keep CPVS issue #170 as a separate unresolved scientific validation blocker.
